claim_87.quote: The TIV antibody response and the MCV4 DT-specific response still follow their day 3 pattern (protein recall response), sharing among the top correlated BTMs plasma cells and immunoglobulin modules (Supplementary Fig. 19,20).

claim_88.claim: In YF-17D vaccinees, plasma cells and immunoglobulin modules as well as memory B cell modules were inversely correlated with antibody titers.
claim_88.quote: Interestingly, these plasma cells and immunoglobulin modules, as well as memory B cell modules, are inversely correlated to antibody titers in YF-17D (Supplementary Fig. 12e, Supplementary Table 2), which is the opposite of what was observed with TIV and MCV4, where there is a positive correlation with the antibody responses (Supplementary Fig. 20).

claim_89.claim: In TIV and MCV4, plasma cells and immunoglobulin modules showed a positive correlation with antibody responses.
claim_89.quote: Interestingly, these plasma cells and immunoglobulin modules, as well as memory B cell modules, are inversely correlated to antibody titers in YF-17D (Supplementary Fig. 12e, Supplementary Table 2), which is the opposite of what was observed with TIV and MCV4, where there is a positive correlation with the antibody responses (Supplementary Fig. 20).

claim_90.claim: T cell activation appeared to be negatively correlated with antibody responses in MPSV4 at day 7.
claim_90.quote: For instance, T cell activation appears to be negatively correlated with antibody responses in MPSV4 (D7) and TIV (D3 and D7), consistent with our previous report 6.

claim_91.claim: T cell activation appeared to be negatively correlated with antibody responses in TIV at days 3 and 7.
claim_91.quote: For instance, T cell activation appears to be negatively correlated with antibody responses in MPSV4 (D7) and TIV (D3 and D7), consistent with our previous report 6.

claim_92.claim: A male-specific module (M240) was negatively correlated with antibody response across these vaccines.
claim_92.quote: A male-specific module (M240) is negatively correlated to antibody response in all these vaccines with varying statistical significance, suggesting a gender bias in antibody production.
